historical_references.reference: Muhazab ibn Sabrah was a prominent companion of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and an early convert to Islam. He participated in several significant battles during the early Islamic era, including the Battle of Uhud (625 AD) and the Battle of Hunayn (630 AD). Muhazab was known for his bravery and dedication to the cause of Islam.

The Battle of Muhaz (or Mu'tah) took place in 629 AD, during the time of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). It was a military expedition sent against the Christian Byzantine forces in Syria, led by the Muslim commander Al-Mundhir ibn Sasan. The battle resulted in a significant victory for the Muslims, but the loss of life and resources was heavy. The name 'Muhaz' is believed to derive from the name of the location where the battle took place, which was called Al-Muhaz.
